facts.authoredFrom: Read from the case's input bytes: grund.toml (version 1, `strict = false`, default kinds and scan) and sub/docs/spec.md. The default `[scan] include` is `["requirements.md", "docs", "e2e", "src"]` from the config root (§FS-config.3.5), and sub/docs is under none of it, so a run given no path, from the root or from sub/docs, and the editor's run at the root read no file: the catalog is empty and FS-001-foo is absent. `check` then earns the empty-scan caution's repo-root message (§FS-check.2.2, §FS-check.2.2.2.1) beside the version caution (§FS-check.checks.config-version-1), both site-less CLI-level lines (§FS-check.2.1.1) in the report's bytewise (path, line, message) order (§FS-errors.4.1, §FS-check.checks.config-version-1.1), the version caution first. `cover --lines` reads the one file it is given (§FS-cover.6.1), so on every variant line 1 of sub/docs/spec.md is still FS-001-foo's. A path argument is read though it lies outside `include` (§FS-scan.path.check): there sub/docs/spec.md declares FS-001-foo, its body to line 3, outside the FS home, which does not exist, so no index rule applies (§FS-check.3.18.7); its marked §FS-999-bar dangles (§FS-check.3.1) and nothing cites FS-001-foo, so it is unused, and JSON findings keep the global path, line, message order (§FS-errors.4.1). Cross-reference emission wraps no unresolved citation (§FS-fmt.6.4), so `fmt` writes nothing. FS-404 is the absent control. `--path-base=invocation` is the case's own manifest call alone (§FS-cli.3.4), where it gives the bytes `relative_paths = false` gives (§FS-config.3.6.1); every other question takes the default base, the config root, so every caution names `grund.toml`.
